solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lovely old mates of Brian Cox last in astronomy

parts.note: before becoming a TV physicist, Brian Cox played keyboards in the 1990s pop band D:Ream

indicators.note: the final letter of the word astronomy is the one taken

explanation.surface: A wistful look back at Brian Cox's former bandmates, finally getting into astronomy as he did.
explanation.walkthrough: D:Ream, the band behind 'Things Can Only Get Better', counted the physicist Brian Cox among its members.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreamy is delightful or wonderful, a colloquial synonym for lovely.

clue.text: What sickly gardenia needs?

indicators.note: an unwell plant name is mixed up, so the letters of gardenia are reordered

explanation.surface: A gardening question about what an ailing gardenia requires.
explanation.walkthrough: Gardenias hate waterlogged soil, so the whole clue both defines and builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterlogged plant suffers root rot, and letting water run away through the soil is the cure.

clue.text: English doctor in Wales knitted jumpers in spring

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go inside the rearranged Wales
the letters of Wales are worked together into a new pattern

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: An English GP in Wales knits woolly sweaters in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumpers' suggests knitted sweaters (British for pullovers); it means leaping young sheep. 'knitted' rearranges the country's name to WELAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Young female sheep born in spring leap about in the fields, so they are springtime jumpers.

clue.text: The look of one who's in pieces

indicators.note: the one is placed inside the chessmen

parts.note: chess pieces are called men
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The appearance of someone falling apart emotionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pieces' looks like distress, but 'pieces' are chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's bearing or expression, the way they look to others.

clue.text: Staunch Tory regularly tortures police officer

indicators.note: taking every other letter of tortures, starting with the first

parts.note: police officers are 'the boys in blue', from the colour of the uniform

explanation.surface: A hardline Conservative is accused of routinely tormenting a constable.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is the Conservative Party colour, and a dyed-in-the-wool loyal party member is described by this phrase.

clue.text: Fellow candidates competing against couples

parts.note: running in a race or election is competing
to mate is to couple or pair up

explanation.surface: Candidates standing for election against married couples.
explanation.definitionFit: In US politics a vice-presidential candidate on the same ticket is the presidential nominee's partner on the ballot.

clue.text: Pick different iron clubs, exploiting chips?

parts.note: to elect is to pick or choose

indicators.note: the word iron in a different form, its letters reordered

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A golfer selects other irons, maybe for chip shots onto the green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chips' suggests golf shots, fitting the irons, but means silicon microchips. 'different' turns IRON into RONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic devices work by means of silicon microchips, so they are exploiting chips.

clue.text: Celeb, say, boring host

indicators.note: drilling into, so the example letters go inside the celebrity

parts.note: a lion is a celebrity, as in a literary lion
eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: A celebrity is dismissed as a dull presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' suggests a presenter, but means a multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion is a vast number, as is a host, both originally armies.

clue.text: By the sound of it, I'll film small opening

indicators.note: the contraction is spoken aloud and written down as it sounds

parts.note: the contraction said quickly sounds like the start of the answer
ET is the Spielberg film about an extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: Someone announces that they will shoot a scene through a tiny aperture.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'I'll' is heard; 'film' gives ET as written.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small reinforced hole for a lace or cord to pass through.

clue.text: Test All About Eve

indicators.note: the letters of All go around the name Eve, enclosing it

explanation.surface: Reads as the title of the 1950 Bette Davis film, All About Eve.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised film title hides the instruction. An A level is the English school-leaving exam taken at about eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: An A level is an examination, a kind of test taken by older school pupils in England.

clue.text: Sweet-talk pair of Europeans living abroad

indicators.note: abroad in its sense of widely scattered or astray, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, so two of them give two Es

explanation.surface: Two expatriates charm their way through life overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigle is to coax or wheedle someone with flattery, which is sweet-talking them.

clue.text: Base local idiots drinking two pints

indicators.note: the idiots take in the measure of liquid, enclosing it

parts.note: header is regional slang, especially Irish, for a crazy person
a quart equals two pints

explanation.surface: Some local fools in their usual pub downing a couple of pints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like an adjective (low) but is the noun for a centre of operations.
explanation.definitionFit: A base is a centre of operations, as is a company or military head office.

clue.text: Close down earmarked stores

indicators.note: the words down earmarked hold, or store, the letters within them

explanation.surface: An instruction to shut down shops that have been earmarked for closure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a verb here, but it is the adjective meaning nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Close in the sense of nearby or not far away is a direct synonym.

clue.text: He left grease around heart of green plant

indicators.note: turned around, so the words left and grease are written backwards together

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
oil is a lubricant used to grease machinery

indicators.note: the central letter of the five-letter word green

explanation.surface: A mechanic leaves greasy marks all over a green plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses PORTOIL to LIOTROP, which follows HE; the middle letter of green, E, ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Heliotrope is a garden flowering shrub with fragrant purple blooms that turn towards the sun.

clue.text: Like bats or lunatics, raving?

indicators.note: wild and incoherent, so the letters of or lunatics are jumbled

explanation.surface: A question comparing bats with madmen, both raving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' also means crazy, matching 'lunatics'; here it means the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats navigate by echolocation, emitting high-pitched calls above human hearing range.

clue.text: Put away vanity and sanction bull

parts.note: to put away food is to eat it greedily, past tense
an ego is a sense of self-importance, close to vanity
to OK something is to approve or sanction it

explanation.surface: Someone renounces vanity and endorses a bull, a peculiar pair of resolutions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull' is short for bullshit: nonsense, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bull is slang for nonsense or meaningless talk, and that is what this word means.

clue.text: Former cost of videos halved?

parts.note: the first half of the word videos is VI D, read as the Roman numeral six and d, the old pre-decimal penny

explanation.walkthrough: Halve 'videos' to VID: VI is the Roman six, d the symbol for an old penny, so VI D is a sum of money in pre-1971 British coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: Before decimalisation in 1971 Britain had a small silver coin worth half a shilling.

clue.text: Old paper and rubbish imported in a distressed state

indicators.note: brought in, so the paper and rubbish go inside the word for old

parts.note: aged means old
the i is a British national newspaper
tat is shoddy rubbish

explanation.surface: Old newspapers and junk brought in, all looking tattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitated means troubled or anxious, a synonym for distressed in the emotional sense.

clue.text: Shocking yet refreshing amusing trait

indicators.note: giving the words amusing trait a fresh arrangement, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A personality quirk is described as both startling and pleasantly funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refreshing' looks like praise for the trait, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something traumatising causes deep distress, so it is shocking in the strongest sense.

clue.text: Authority hide boat with no bow

indicators.note: the bow is the front of a boat, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a coracle is a small round boat traditionally made of hide stretched on a frame

explanation.surface: An official orders a boat hidden that has lost its front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like a verb but is the animal skin a coracle is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is an infallible authority or expert whose pronouncements are trusted.

clue.text: The Spanish up in Middlesbrough dance

indicators.note: placed inside the nickname

parts.note: Boro is the nickname of Middlesbrough football club

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading the word backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish dance is performed in the north-east English town of Middlesbrough.
explanation.definitionFit: The bolero is a Spanish dance in triple time, also known from Ravel's orchestral piece.

clue.text: Back entry to show division in church

indicators.note: reading the word for entry backwards

parts.note: a door is an entry into a building
to screen a film or programme is to show it

explanation.surface: Instructions to use the rear door to see a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood screen is the carved partition separating the nave from the chancel in many old churches.

clue.text: Rained a little, leading to flood briefly

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the synonym for flood is lost

parts.note: a spate is a river in flood

explanation.surface: A short shower of rain soon leads to a flash flood.
explanation.definitionFit: When it spits it rains lightly in scattered drops, and the past tense of spit fits rained a little.

clue.text: Titled woman furious about drug

indicators.note: turned about, so the word for furious is written backwards

parts.note: mad means furious
E is short for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A noblewoman is enraged by a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a dame is a woman awarded a knighthood-equivalent honour, a title like Sir.

clue.text: Son enthralled by daily soap

indicators.note: held captive within, so the son's letter sits inside the cleaner

parts.note: a daily is a British cleaner who comes in each day

explanation.surface: A boy is captivated by a daily TV soap opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soap' suggests a TV drama, and 'daily' a newspaper; both are misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap is a substance that cleans, so it is one type of product used for washing.

clue.text: Regulation rejected by head cabinetmaker

definitions.note: here meaning the material a cabinet is made of, not the craftsman

indicators.note: turned back, so the word for regulation is written backwards

parts.note: a law is a regulation
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A chief furniture maker turns down a new rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cabinetmaker' looks like a person but means the wood from which cabinets are made.
explanation.definitionFit: Walnut is a prized hardwood for fine furniture, so it is what makes many cabinets.

clue.text: Troops interrupt duty to get rid of spirit

indicators.note: the troops break into the word for duty, sitting inside it

parts.note: excise is a duty levied on goods
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers disrupt customs work to confiscate smuggled liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests alcohol, fitting the excise surface, but means a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: To exorcise is to drive out an evil spirit or ghost from a person or place.

clue.text: Top eastern ambassador visits poor

indicators.note: the letters go in to call on, sitting inside the word for poor

parts.note: bad means poor in quality
HE is His Excellency, the form of address for an ambassador

explanation.surface: A senior Eastern envoy calls on the needy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective meaning senior; it is the slang verb meaning to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is slang for executing them, and cutting off the head is one way.
